extracted.intended_audience: Carpentries instructor trainers and volunteer instructors (people preparing to teach Carpentries-style lessons)
extracted.subtask_description: A glossary of pedagogical terms used in Carpentries instructor training, providing short definitions and cross-references to guide lesson design, delivery, and feedback practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Equal access to learning opportunities regardless of learners’ physical abilities or other attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic Task
rubrics_metrics.description: A task which contains important elements of things that learners would do in real life (i.e. non-classroom situations). To be authentic, a task should require learners to construct their own answers rather than choose among provided answers, and to work with the same tools and data they would use in real life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chunking
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of grouping related concepts together so that they can be stored and processed as a single unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognitive Load
rubrics_metrics.description: Cognitive load is the amount of mental effort required to solve a problem. Cognitive load theory divides this effort into intrinsic, extraneous, and germane, and holds that people learn faster and better when extraneous load is reduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentions the three types of load (intrinsic, extraneous, germane) and emphasizes reducing extraneous load to speed and improve learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community of Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A self-perpetuating group of people who share and develop a craft or occupation, such as knitters, musicians, or programmers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent Practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Someone who can do normal tasks with normal effort under normal circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept Map
rubrics_metrics.description: A picture of a mental model in which concepts are nodes in a graph and relationships are (labelled) arcs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of observing performance of a task while doing it in order to improve ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic Power
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which a wrong answer to a question or exercise tells the instructor what misconceptions a particular learner has.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational Psychology
rubrics_metrics.description: The study of how people learn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effort-based Praise
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing positive feedback to learners that recognises and rewards their hard work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also improvement-based praise and performance-based praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error Framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting errors as an integral part of the learning process and using them as teaching opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert
rubrics_metrics.description: Someone who can diagnose and handle unusual situations, knows when the usual rules do not apply, and tends to recognise solutions rather than reasoning to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also competent practitioner and novice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert Awareness Gap
rubrics_metrics.description: The inability of experts to empathise with novices who are encountering concepts or practices for the first time. Often referred to as expert blind spot in the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faded Example
rubrics_metrics.description: A series of examples in which a steadily increasing number of key steps are blanked out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed Mindset
rubrics_metrics.description: The belief that an ability is innate, and that failure is due to a lack of some necessary attribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluid Representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to move quickly between different models of a problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formative Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment that takes place during a lesson in order to give both the learner and the instructor feedback on actual understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth Mindset
rubrics_metrics.description: The belief that ability comes with practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impostor Syndrome
rubrics_metrics.description: A feeling of insecurity about one’s accomplishments that manifests as a fear of being exposed as a fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement-based Praise
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing positive feedback to learners that recognises and rewards improvements they have made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also effort-based praise and performance-based praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Working actively to include people with diverse backgrounds and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inquiry-Based Learning
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of allowing learners to ask their own questions, set their own goals, and find their own path through a subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jugyokenkyu
rubrics_metrics.description: See lesson study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alias/reference to lesson study (a collaborative lesson-planning and observation practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lateral Knowledge Transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The “accidental” transfer of knowledge that occurs when an instructor is teaching one thing, and the learner picks up another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learner Profile
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief description of a typical target learner for a lesson that includes their general background, what they already know, what they want to do, how the lesson will help them, and any special needs they might have.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning Objective
rubrics_metrics.description: What a lesson is trying to achieve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson Study
rubrics_metrics.description: The process in which instructors collaboratively plan lessons, observe each other’s teaching, and discuss teaching experiences in order to learn from each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live Coding
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of teaching programming by writing software in front of learners as the lesson progresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-Term Memory
rubrics_metrics.description: The part of memory that stores information for long periods of time. Long-term memory is very large, but slow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental Model
rubrics_metrics.description: A representation of a person’s knowledge and thought processes about a topic or domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minute Cards
rubrics_metrics.description: A feedback technique in which learners spend a minute writing one positive thing about a lesson (e.g., one thing they have learned) and one negative thing (e.g., a question that still hasn’t been answered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novice
rubrics_metrics.description: Someone who has not yet built a usable mental model of a domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also competent practitioner and expert.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-Up, One-Down
rubrics_metrics.description: A feedback technique in which learners take turns giving positive and negative feedback without repeating anything that has been said before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participatory Live Coding
rubrics_metrics.description: A style of teaching where the instructor live codes and the learners “code along”.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance-based Praise
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing positive feedback to learners that focuses on whether they have attained the correct answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also effort-based praise and performance-based praise (cross-references present on page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perseverance
rubrics_metrics.description: The trait of persisting in the face of difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent Memory
rubrics_metrics.description: see long-term memory

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausible Distractor
rubrics_metrics.description: A wrong answer to a multiple-choice question that will seem to some students to be correct due to a misconception they hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflective Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: see deliberate practice

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaffolding
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra material provided to early-stage learners to help them solve problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-Term Memory
rubrics_metrics.description: The part of memory that briefly stores information that can be directly accessed by consciousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stereotype Threat
rubrics_metrics.description: A situation in which people feel that they are at risk of being held to stereotypes of their social group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summative Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment that takes place at the end of a lesson to tell whether the desired learning has taken place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working Memory
rubrics_metrics.description: see short-term memory
